Once upon a time a boy called Jack lived with his mother in a little cottage.
They were very poor.
All they had left was a cow named Milky-White, and the milk had run dry.
We must sell the cow, Jack,
said Mother.
Take her to market and bring home a good price.
On the way Jack met a funny little Peddler.
That is a fine cow,
said Peddler.
I will give you five magic beans for her.
Magic beans?
said Jack.
He thought it was a wonderful bargain, so he handed over Milky-White and ran home with the beans.
Five beans?
Oh, Jack, how silly you are!
She threw the beans out of the window and sent Jack to bed.
In the morning Jack looked out of the window.
A giant beanstalk had grown up in the night, so tall that it went right up into the clouds.
Jack began to climb.
Up and up he went, past the birds and into the clouds.
At the top he found a long road and a huge castle.
A giant woman opened the door.
Oh dear, my husband does not like visitors,
said Giant's Wife.
But you look so hungry that I will give you some bread first.
Boom, boom, boom!
The whole castle shook.
Fee, fi, fo, fum!
said Giant.
I smell a boy!
Nonsense, dear,
It is only the sheep.
She hid Jack in the cupboard, and the Giant sat down to eat.
After supper the Giant took out a bag of gold coins and counted them.
Soon he began to nod, and then he was fast asleep and snoring.
Jack crept out of the cupboard, grabbed the bag of gold and ran down the beanstalk as fast as he could.
Look, Mother!
We are rich!
When the gold was spent, Jack climbed the beanstalk again.
This time the Giant had a little hen that laid golden eggs.
Lay!
said Giant, and the hen laid a golden egg.
When the Giant fell asleep, Jack tucked the hen under his arm and tiptoed away.
Jack went up a third time.
The Giant had a golden harp that played by itself.
Jack took it, but the harp cried out.
Master, master!
said Harp.
The Giant woke up and ran after him.
Jack slid down the beanstalk as fast as he could.
The Giant tried to follow, but the beanstalk wobbled and swayed.
Oh dear, I am too scared to climb down,
So he went back to his castle in the clouds and never came down again.
Jack and his mother lived happily ever after, with the little hen and the golden harp.
